# Multi-Step Registration Form Accessibility Design Plan > **For Claude:** Use a11y-planner protocol. Review with a11y-critic after implementation. > **Compliance target:** WCAG 2.2 AA > **Users who need accessibility:** Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver), keyboard-only users, low vision users, cognitive accessibility users (error load management) > **Assistive technologies:** NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver, keyboard-only navigation, screen magnifier **Feature:** Multi-step healthcare portal registration form with inline validation, step-level error summaries, and cross-step consolidated error handling. **Risk Level:** High **Component/Page Type:** Multi-Step Form Wizard with Dynamic Validation & Error Communication --- ## Scope & Context This plan covers the accessibility design for a four-step registration form (Personal Info → Insurance Details → Medical History → Review/Submit). The form uses React Hook Form (RHF) for state management and currently implements visual error treatments (red borders, red text) without any programmatic ARIA attributes or screen reader communication. **Key Accessibility Gaps to Address:** - Error states are visually indicated but invisible to assistive technology (`aria-invalid` missing, no `aria-describedby`) - Dynamic error summary panel appears without focus movement or live region announcement - Blur-time validation lacks a non-interruptive announcement strategy - Cross-step consolidated errors on final submit lack navigation + focus coordination - Color is currently the sole error indicator (fails WCAG 1.4.1) **Constraints:** RHF must remain as the form state engine. Visual error treatments (red border, red text) must be preserved. Real-time inline validation on blur is a product requirement. Error summary placement at the top of each step is fixed. --- ## Semantic Structure Plan The form must use native HTML form semantics with proper landmark and grouping structure. RHF's `
` wrapper will remain, but internal structure requires explicit semantic landmarks for screen readers. ### Structure Diagram ```html

Healthcare Portal Registration

    3. ...

Personal Information

Error Summary

  • First Name: [error message]
Personal Details First name is required
``` **Design Decisions & WCAG Citations:** - `
` per step with `aria-labelledby` linking to step heading: WCAG 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (programmatic association of structure) - `
`/`` grouping fields by logical category: WCAG 1.3.1 (semantic grouping for screen readers) - Error summary uses `role="alert"` + `aria-live="assertive"`: WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (urgent dynamic content must be announced) - Skip link to `#registration-main` at document top: WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks --- ## Interaction Pattern Design Every interactive element maps to an established APG pattern or standard HTML interaction model. ### Interactive Elements Table | Widget | APG Pattern / Standard | Keyboard Model | ARIA Attributes | WCAG Citation | |--------|------------------------|----------------|-----------------|---------------| | Step Navigation Buttons | APG Tab Panel (if tabs) / Standard Button | Tab to button, Enter/Space to activate | `aria-controls`, `aria-current="step"` (active), `aria-disabled` (completed steps) | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Form Inputs (text, select, date) | APG Text Input / Select | Tab to focus, Enter/Space activates buttons, not inputs | `aria-invalid`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-required` (if native required omitted), `aria-errormessage` (optional) | 1.3.1 Info & Relationships, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Next/Back/Submit Buttons | APG Button | Tab to focus, Enter/Space to activate | `type="submit"` or `type="button"`, `aria-disabled` during async validation | 2.1.1 Keyboard, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Error Summary Links | Standard Anchor | Tab to link, Enter to navigate | `href="#field-id"`, `role="link"` (implicit) | 2.4.4 Link Purpose In Context | | Error Summary Panel | APG Alert / Live Region | Not interactive; focus moves here programmatically | `role="alert"`, `aria-live="assertive"`, `hidden` when empty | 4.1.3 Status Messages, 4.1.2 Name Role Value | **Screen Reader Announcement Strategy:** - **On field focus:** Screen reader announces label + role + value + state (e.g., "First Name, edit text, required") - **On blur validation error:** Error message is associated via `aria-describedby`. Screen readers automatically read it when focus leaves the field. No separate live region needed for inline errors (avoids interruption). - **On step advancement with errors:** Summary panel appears → `role="alert"` announces "3 errors on this page" + reads list items. Focus moves to summary. - **On cross-step consolidation:** Same pattern as step-level summary, but spans all steps. --- ## Focus Management Plan Focus movement is the most critical failure point in multi-step forms with dynamic validation. 1. **Default Tab Order:** Follows visual top-to-bottom, left-to-right reading order per WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order. DOM order matches visual order. 2. **Blur-Time Validation (Inline):** - **DO NOT move focus automatically** when a field blurs with an error. This is disruptive and breaks user flow. - Keep focus on the blurred field so the user can immediately correct it, or allow natural tab progression. - Error message appears below field; `aria-describedby` handles programmatic association. 3. **Step Advancement with Errors:** - When user clicks "Next" and validation fails: Focus moves to the error summary panel (`summaryRef.current.focus()`). - Summary panel uses `role="alert"` + `aria-live="assertive"` to announce errors immediately. - User can Tab through summary links to jump to invalid fields. 4. **Error Summary Link Navigation:** - Links use `href="#field-id"` for scroll/navigate. - On click, a utility function executes: `scrollToElement(target) → target.setAttribute('tabindex', '-1') → target.focus()`. - Screen reader announces "Navigated to [field name]" via a polite live region or focus event. 5. **Cross-Step Consolidation (Final Submit):** - When final submit fails, focus moves to the consolidated error summary at the top of the Review/Submit step. - Links in the list use `href="#step-X-field-id"` to navigate back to the correct step and field. - If steps are conditionally rendered (not in DOM), links must trigger a step switch first, then focus the field after mount. 6. **Focus Indicators:** Double-ring focus indicator (`outline: 2px solid #005fcc; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(0,95,252,0.3)`) visible at all zoom levels per WCAG 2.4.7. 7. **Skip Link:** First focusable element is "Skip to registration form" link targeting `#registration-main`. --- ## State Communication Design Every state must be communicated visually AND programmatically. Color alone fails WCAG 1.4.1. ### State Communication Table | State | Visual Indicator | Programmatic Indicator | ARIA Attribute / Mechanism | WCAG Citation | |-------|-----------------|----------------------|----------------------------|---------------| | Valid (default) | Default border, no icon, neutral label color | `aria-invalid="false"` (or absent), no error message visible | `aria-invalid="false"` (implicit), `aria-describedby` points to hidden span | 4.1.2 Name Role Value | | Invalid (inline/blur) | Red left border (3px), red text, ⚠️ icon, label turns red | `aria-invalid="true"`, error message visible below input | `aria-invalid="true"`, `aria-describedby="error-{field}"` on input, `id="error-{field}"` on span | 1.4.1 Use of Color, 3.3.1 Error Identification | | Invalid (submit-time) | Same as inline + error summary appears at top | Summary panel visible, focus moves to it | `role="alert"`, `aria-live="assertive"` on summary, `hidden` attribute toggled off | 4.1.3 Status Messages, 2.4.3 Focus Order | | Required field | Asterisk (*) next to label, red border when empty | `required` attribute on input (native) or `aria-required="true"` | Native `required` preferred; `aria-required="true"` if native omitted | 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions | | Loading/Submitting | Button shows spinner, disabled state | Button visually dimmed, cursor: wait | `aria-disabled="true"`, `disabled` attribute, `aria-busy="true"` on form | 4.1.2 Name Role Value, 4.1.3 Status Messages | **Blur-Time Announcement Strategy:** - **Recommended approach:** Rely on `aria-describedby` for inline errors. When focus leaves the field, screen readers automatically read the associated error message. This is non-interruptive and standard per WCAG 4.1.3. - **Alternative (if product requires explicit announcement):** Use a dedicated `aria-live="polite"` region at the bottom of the step that updates with a 500ms delay after blur. Polite ensures it waits for screen reader to finish current utterance. Never use `assertive` for blur validation. **Non-Color Error Indicator:** - Add a warning icon (⚠️ or ✗) positioned left of the input or inside the input field. - Add text prefix "Error:" or "Invalid:" to error messages. - Cite WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color: "Color is not the only visual means of conveying information." --- ## Visual Accessibility Plan 1. **Color Contrast:** Error text and borders must meet 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors (WCAG 1.4.3). Red border (#d32f2f) on white background = 5.9:1 ✓. Error text must be dark enough for readability. 2. **Non-Color Alternatives:** Every error state uses: (1) Red border + red text, (2) Warning icon (⚠️), (3) Text label ("Error:" or "Invalid:"). Color is never the sole indicator. 3. **Font Sizing & Zoom:** All form elements use `rem` units. Base font 16px. Tested at 200% zoom per WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text and 1.4.10 Reflow. No horizontal scroll at 320px viewport (1280px at 400%). 4. **Animation & Motion:** Error summary fades in with `transition: opacity 0.2s ease`. Respects `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` by disabling transition and showing instantly. WCAG 2.3.3 Animation from Interactions. 5. **Touch Targets:** Next/Back/Submit buttons minimum 44x44 CSS pixels per WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum). Spacing between buttons ≥ 8px to prevent accidental activation. 6. **Focus Indicator Visibility:** Double-ring focus style (`outline` + `box-shadow`) ensures visibility on light/dark backgrounds and in Windows High Contrast Mode. Framework CSS overrides handled via high-specificity selectors or `!important` where necessary. --- ## Content Accessibility Plan 1. **Error Message Clarity (WCAG 3.3.1 & 3.3.3):** - Specific: "Email address is missing" not "Invalid input" - Actionable: "Enter a valid email address including @ symbol" - Location-aware: Error messages appear immediately below the field they reference 2. **Form Labels:** Every input has an associated `
